Be part of a team that unleashes the power of leading-edge technologies to help improve the health and well-being of those most vulnerable in our country and communities. Working at Gainwell carries its rewards. You’ll have an incredible opportunity to grow your career in a company that values work flexibility, learning, and career development. You’ll add to your technical credentials and certifications while enjoying a generous, flexible vacation policy and educational assistance. We also have comprehensive leadership and technical development academies to help build your skills and capabilities.
Summary
As an Early Career C#/.NET Developer (Healthcare Applications) at Gainwell, you can contribute your skills as we harness the power of technology to help our clients improve the health and well-being of the members they serve — a community’s most vulnerable. Connect your passion with purpose, teaming with people who thrive on finding innovative solutions to some of healthcare’s biggest challenges. Here are the details on this position.
The SUR Developer I is an entry-level software development role responsible for supporting the design, development, testing, maintenance, and enhancement of applications supporting the Surveillance and Utilization Review (SUR) program. Under the guidance of senior developers and technical leads, this position contributes to application development, defect resolution, system enhancements, and production support activities.
Your role in our mission
Develop, test, and maintain application components using Oracle PL/SQL, C#, and ASP.NET.
Assist in the analysis of business and technical requirements.
Create and modify database objects including packages, procedures, functions, and queries.
Support application troubleshooting, defect remediation, and root cause analysis.
Participate in code reviews and follow established coding standards and SDLC processes.
Collaborate with business analysts, testers, and senior developers to deliver system enhancements.
Document technical designs, code changes, and operational procedures.
Support production issues and participate in on-call activities as assigned.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and application modernization efforts.
What We're Looking For
0 to 2 years of experience in software development, application support, or a related technical role, with a Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Software Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent experience.
Basic programming and database experience with Oracle Database, PL/SQL, C#, ASP.NET, SQL, and relational database concepts.
Understanding of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), software development best practices, web application development, and troubleshooting methodologies.
Strong analytical, problem solving, communication, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team environment and support business objectives.
Preferred experience or exposure to SSRS, Entity Framework, Azure DevOps/Git, Visual Studio, and healthcare, Medicaid, or government systems.
What You Should Expect In This Role
Fully remote opportunity with the option to work anywhere within the United States
Opportunities to travel through your work (0-10%)
Willingness to work a flexible schedule to accommodate business needs and travel as required
Video cameras must be used during all interviews, as well as during the initial week of orientation
The deadline to submit applications for this posting is December 30, 2026
The pay range for this position is $46,600.00 - $66,600.00 per year, however, the base pay offered may vary depending on geographic region, internal equity, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. Put your passion to work at Gainwell. You’ll have the opportunity to grow your career in a company that values work flexibility, learning, and career development. All salaried, full-time candidates are eligible for our generous, flexible vacation policy, a 401(k) employer match, comprehensive health benefits, and educational assistance. We also have a variety of leadership and technical development academies to help build your skills and capabilities.
We believe nothing is impossible when you bring together people who care deeply about making healthcare work better for everyone. Build your career with Gainwell, an industry leader. You’ll be joining a company where collaboration, innovation, and inclusion fuel our growth. Learn more about Gainwell at our company website and visit our Careers site for all available job role openings.
Gainwell Technologies is an Equal Opportunity Employer, where all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical condition), age, sexual orientation, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. Gainwell Technologies defines “wages” and “wage rates” to include “all forms of pay, including, but not limited to, salary, overtime pay, bonuses, stock, stock options, profit sharing and bonus plans, life insurance, vacation and holiday pay, cleaning or gasoline allowances, hotel accommodations, reimbursement for travel expenses, and benefits.

About Devroute
Devroute is a software company in Karachi that builds web and mobile products for clients, mostly in the United States. We're a small team where engineers own real features, ship to production, and work directly on international projects.
About the Role
We're looking for a Python Developer with hands-on experience with FastAPI to join our growing engineering team. You'll build and scale the backend systems behind client products, including AI-powered applications. If you like clean APIs, well-designed databases, and solving performance problems, we'd like to hear from you.
Job Details
• Location: Karachi, Pakistan (On-site)
• Job Type: Full-time
• Shift: Night shift
• Experience: 2+ years
What You'll Do
• Develop and maintain scalable backend applications using Python and FastAPI
• Design, build, and integrate RESTful APIs
• Work with PostgreSQL and optimize database queries
• Implement authentication, authorization, and security best practices
• Integrate third-party APIs and services
• Collaborate with frontend developers and other engineering teams
• Troubleshoot, debug, and improve application performance
• Write clean, maintainable, well-documented code
What You'll Need
• Strong proficiency in Python and FastAPI
• Experience with PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, and Alembic
• Understanding of asynchronous programming
• Experience with Pydantic and RESTful API architecture
• Familiarity with Git and version control workflows
• Understanding of database design and query optimization
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Nice to Have
• Experience with AWS and Docker
• Familiarity with Redis, Celery, and background task processing
• Experience with AI/LLM integrations
• Understanding of CI/CD pipelines and microservices architecture
• Experience with multi-tenant applications
What We Offer
• Competitive salary based on experience
• Work on international projects and AI-powered applications
• Professional growth and career development
• A collaborative and supportive work environment

About the Company
Stone Grid builds StoneApp, the ERP platform that 100+ stone and countertop fabricators across North America use to run their entire business, from quoting and CAD to production, scheduling and installation. Stone fabrication is a large, hands-on industry that still runs largely on paper, spreadsheets and disconnected systems. We're on a mission to revolutionize it: using AI and automation to transform how fabricators quote, plan, cut and install, and building the modern platform the industry runs on. Customers also bring us in as experts: we consult on their operational problems and build software solutions for them. We're a small, remote-first team that ships like a much bigger one, because every engineer builds with AI coding agents.
About the Role
This is an engineering role first: most of your time goes to building and shipping StoneApp features. You'll also work directly with fabricators, on calls and on-site, as a trusted technical advisor. You'll learn how their shops run, diagnose their problems, and shape the features and paid solutions that fix them.
Location and travel: Fully remote within the US, with travel to customer sites a couple of times a quarter.
Responsibilities
Build and ship features across React/TypeScript and .NET, using AI coding agents
Consult with customers: understand their operations, recommend solutions and help scope paid projects
Visit shops occasionally to learn the industry firsthand and help with rollouts
Turn what you learn into clear requirements, then build the solution
Own production issues with customers through to resolution
Qualifications
New grads and early-career engineers welcome
We care more about what you've built than years of experience
US-based and authorized to work in the US. We're unable to sponsor work visas at this time
Required Skills
Strong engineering fundamentals: you break down messy problems and ship working software
Excellent spoken and written English, and confidence advising customers directly
A fast learner who gets comfortable in a new industry quickly
Ability or interest in building with AI coding agents (we'll train you)
Willing to travel a couple of times a quarter
Preferred Skills
Consulting, implementation or solutions engineering experience
ERP, manufacturing or construction software
React/TypeScript, .NET or SQL
Pay range and compensation package
What we offer: remote-first work with occasional travel, real ownership of products and consulting projects fabricators rely on daily, hands-on AI and automation work, and room to grow
Compensation: $60,000–$120,000 base, depending on experience. New grads typically start toward the lower end of the range
Benefits: paid time off and reimbursement for work-related expenses (travel, AI coding tools and more)
Hiring process: a short application question, a take-home project (2–3 hours), one interview, and a paid 1–2 week trial project
Equal Opportunity Statement
Stone Grid is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

A resignation letter is rarely just a change in personnel. To the market, it is a signal.
 
In Part 1 of my two-part article on Regulation 30, I look at what must happen when a director, a KMP, a member of Senior Management or the Compliance Officer leaves:
 
🔹The clock: 24 hours for a resignation, 12 hours for a termination, and a later Board meeting does not restart it.
🔹The letter: detailed reasons in the person's own words, within 7 days.
🔹The vacancy: 3 months for most offices, up to 6 months where regulatory approval is needed.
🔹The trap: the "sanitised annexure", where the company's summary is softer than the letter it summarises. Five recent filings show it.
 
With real 2025–26 filings and a one-page ‘Regulation 30 Resignation Compliance matrix’ for your Board pack.
 
Part 2, on Auditors and an absent MD or CEO, follows on 24 November.
 
How does your Board handle a resignation letter that raises concerns?
